we designed a wearable, portable, and autonomous multi-gas sensor system with a low power consumption, high sensitivity and selectivity, and rapid response time.

we have developed a system that integrates an array of electrochemical sensors and a low-power, multi-mode electrochemical instrument circuit with an embedded signal-processing algorithm to enable real-time gas classification and estimation of concentration within a real-world gas mixture.
we have designed, fabricated, and demonstrated a wearable multi-analyte microsystem for environmental monitoring.

developing a low-cost, portable and autonomous system capable of real-time monitoring of multiple hazardous gases in the environment.
developing and demonstrating a wearable autonomous gas sensor system that can detect and quantify multiple analytes in real-time and provide an early warning for health and safety threats.
the development and integration of a low-power, low-cost, portable and wearable multi-analyte chemical sensor array for real time environmental monitoring.

this research is the first step towards a new generation of autonomous, wearable, and multi-gas sensing system that will enable the real-time monitoring of the environment for health and safety applications.

this work represents a significant advancement in the state-of-the-art for wearable gas sensing systems.

the wearable autonomous microsystem with the electrochemical sensor array for real time health and safety monitoring has a great potential in the future.
we developed and demonstrated a wearable autonomous microsystem with an electrochemical gas sensor that provides a real-time health and environmental monitoring capability.
